problem_type: Editor gestures and tool receipts lose the identity of the next user action
symptom: Composition-end Enter and slash with a chip submit unintended actions. Two presses can confirm two offers. A generate call waiting in preflight is folded as streaming.
direct_cause: Capture treated keyCode 229 as plain Enter, chip eligibility overrode slash, and an unscoped button ref could activate each new primary. The receipt joined the operation ID to Pi runningTools, which excludes before_tool.
class_root: Neither input dispatch nor tool presentation binds the waiting user action to its actual owner.
affected_population: Creators using the resident panel in the sidebar, dock or floating shell and the shared panel in the design lab.
entry_points: Unsettled tool calls in laneViewModel and collapsed work history
internal_only_reason: The approved Nomi boards and design system specify the gesture and the existing tool-state vocabulary.
invariants: Plain empty Enter activates only the mounted waiting spend action. Drafts, IME, repeated keys and library navigation cannot authorize it.
Waiting receipts remain visible with their existing localized approval label. Concurrent work keeps its own progress.
A quote may be confirmed from the composer once. A retry requires direct interaction. A subsequent quote accepts Enter after it has been visible for 500 ms.
An external card hold and a gate approval remain distinct. Only the held toolCallIds enter the receipt projection.

door_reduction.why_not: The docks and design fixtures mount the shared cards or the whole panel. Single receipts and work history consume the same tool facts. The language resources supply the existing labels. The desktop host owns the actual wait. The card hook reads the quote and each mounted panel consumes the displayed identity.

generality_proof: All resident layouts use the same panel. The displayed spend quoteId covers the project, operation, presentation and shot revisions independently of handoff progress. Lane approvals use the pending toolCallId. The gate publishes all active holds by call ID so concurrent calls and old calls on the same plan keep their own statuses.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Dispatch editor Enter to a single action. An empty editor can delegate to the waiting spend button in its own panel.
Associate an unresolved tool call with its own waiting spend offer or pending tool approval.
Consume a displayed confirmation identity once and protect the transition to a subsequent offer.
Publish and clear the call IDs of outside-card waits with the lifetime of the holds.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Mounts the common panel, spend slot and draft owner in the resident shell.
Full-panel fixtures render the same keyboard boundary and button.
Question-local Enter advances answers while focus is in the question card.

recurrence.reason: Every later conversation can present another offer during text composition, library navigation or parallel tool execution.
same_class_scan: door-map V4Intervention, V4SpendBar and AgentPanelV4Composer identified the resident and design-lab surfaces.
Traced laneViewModel and collapseV4Flow through ToolStatusIcon against generate waiting in laneExtendedDesktopPorts.
The desktop generate preflight borrows a hold from the gate. The ordinary spend approval stays in pending. The pending quote and lane approval are the two identities consumed by the panel.

prevention.invariant: Each editor gesture belongs to one active control.
prevention.failure_mode: Composition and slash stay in the editor. A consumed quote, a retry, or a freshly switched quote cannot spend through accidental Enter. Direct interaction with an enabled button remains available.
prevention.strategy: Capture composition before picker/send/confirm, veto bare slash before chip eligibility, and bind empty Enter to a consumable quote on the rendered button. Read call identity from the gate before folding the receipt.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed unconditional button activation, chip-first slash eligibility, and renderer inference of a held call from runningTools and operationId.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The issue concerns application dispatch and projection. React already exposes native keyboard events and button refs.

migration: All changes are read-time or live UI decisions. Existing drafts, settings and tool results retain their stored format.
residual_risks: The coordinator verifies both locales in the real window. No paid request was exercised.
